questions.question: According to the passage, what is at the core of unbelief that fights against the truths of Islam?
questions.answer: It is mainly built on denying, not knowing, and rejecting the truth.

questions.question: How is belief described in contrast to unbelief?
questions.answer: Belief is described as real knowledge, affirmation, and a sound judgment.

questions.question: Why can unbelief sometimes look like something positive even though it is not?
questions.answer: It may seem like a firm position, but in reality it is based on rejection and emptiness rather than true knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage say every denying side of belief points toward?
questions.answer: It points toward a real positive truth or hides one behind it.

questions.question: When can a person’s unbelief be counted in one way as a kind of mistaken knowledge?
questions.answer: When the person struggles to treat false negation as if it were something accepted and settled in the mind.

questions.question: What is unbelief called when it is simply refusal, denial, and not admitting the truth?
questions.answer: It is called complete ignorance and a total lack of judgment.

questions.question: What is the first main kind of conviction connected to unbelief?
questions.answer: It is a false belief that does not pay attention to the truths of Islam and stays within its own mistaken view.

questions.question: Why is that first kind said to be outside the discussion?
questions.answer: Because it does not directly fight the truths of faith in the way the passage is focusing on.

questions.question: What is the second main kind of unbelief?
questions.answer: It is the kind that stands against the truths of belief and tries to oppose them.

questions.question: What is the first variety within this second kind?
questions.answer: It is simple non-acceptance, meaning a person does not agree with the truth but has not formed a full judgment.

questions.question: Why is simple non-acceptance described as a kind of ignorance?
questions.answer: Because it happens without a real settled judgment and is more like not knowing than proving anything.

questions.question: What is the second variety within the opposing kind of unbelief?
questions.answer: It is inwardly agreeing with non-existence and treating negation like a real position.

questions.question: Why does this second variety involve judgment more than simple non-acceptance?
questions.answer: Because the person takes a side in the heart and adopts denial as a chosen conviction.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It is denying that a certain thing exists in one specific place or direction.

questions.question: Why can that first type of negation be proven?
questions.answer: Because it is limited and specific, so it can be checked.

questions.question: What is the second type of negation?
questions.answer: It is denying broad matters of belief and sacred truths connected to the world, creation, the hereafter, and all times.

questions.question: Why can this second type of negation not be proven?
questions.answer: Because proving it would require complete knowledge of the whole universe, the next life, and every part of time.

questions.question: What basic difference does the passage make between unbelief and belief?
questions.answer: Unbelief is tied to denial and lack, while belief is tied to knowledge and affirmation.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying belief is related to “being”?
questions.answer: It means belief is connected to real truth and a true recognition of what exists.

questions.question: What does it mean that unbelief is related to “non-being”?
questions.answer: It means unbelief is based on rejection and absence rather than solid truth.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the hidden side of the truths found in belief?
questions.answer: It says that when belief denies something false, that denial actually opens the way to a real truth.

questions.question: In what situation is unbelief considered a wrong kind of knowledge instead of total ignorance?
questions.answer: When a person forms a settled but false conviction and treats denial as if it were an accepted fact.

questions.question: What makes non-acceptance easier than building a false conviction?
questions.answer: A person can refuse to accept something without doing the harder work of forming a full argument or judgment.

questions.question: Into how many main groups are the convictions behind unbelief divided?
questions.answer: They are divided into two main groups.

questions.question: How is the first group described?
questions.answer: It is a mistaken and unfair belief that ignores the truths of Islam without directly dealing with them in this discussion.

questions.question: How is the second group described?
questions.answer: It is the group that actively resists and argues against the truths of belief.

questions.question: What are the two varieties inside this second group?
questions.answer: One is simple refusal to accept, and the other is accepting non-existence as a conviction.

questions.question: Which of these two varieties does not include a real judgment?
questions.answer: Simple refusal to accept does not include a real judgment.

questions.question: Which variety includes inner support for denial?
questions.answer: Accepting non-existence includes inner support for denial.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this second variety is forced to support its own negation?
questions.answer: Because once someone chooses denial as a side, that person tries to treat it like a position that must be defended.

questions.question: Which kind of negation is not the main focus of the passage because it can be demonstrated?
questions.answer: Denying the presence of a certain thing in a certain place is not the main focus.

questions.question: Which kind of negation is the real problem in the passage?
questions.answer: The real problem is denying large, sacred truths that cover all existence, the hereafter, and the ages.

questions.question: What would someone need in order to prove that broad kind of denial?
questions.answer: That person would need unlimited knowledge covering the universe, the next life, and all of time.

questions.question: What overall lesson does this passage teach about strong claims against faith?
questions.answer: It teaches that broad denials of faith are not easy to prove and often rest on ignorance or false judgment instead of true knowledge.

questions.question: What three words best summarize the foundation of unbelief in this passage?
questions.answer: Denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What three ideas best summarize belief in this passage?
questions.answer: Knowledge, affirmation, and judgment.

questions.question: Why does the passage say unbelief can seem like a kind of affirmation?
questions.answer: Because some people try to present their rejection as if it were a real conclusion.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is unbelief actually like beneath that appearance?
questions.answer: It is really built on rejection and absence, not on firm truth.

questions.question: How can a negative part of belief still lead to something positive?
questions.answer: It can block falsehood and point a person toward a true reality behind it.

questions.question: What is the difference between mistaken acceptance and simple denial?
questions.answer: Mistaken acceptance is a false judgment a person adopts, while simple denial is refusing to accept without reaching a real judgment.

questions.question: Which kind of unbelief is said to have no concern with the discussion?
questions.answer: The kind that keeps to its own false belief and does not directly enter the argument being examined.

questions.question: What kind of unbelief is the discussion mainly concerned with?
questions.answer: It is concerned with the kind that opposes the truths of belief.

questions.question: Why is non-acceptance called a type of ignorance?
questions.answer: Because it lacks a formed conclusion and is mainly a failure to know or agree.

questions.question: Why is accepting non-existence more serious than non-acceptance?
questions.answer: Because it is not just hesitation or refusal; it is choosing denial as a belief.

questions.question: What does it mean that this second variety “takes the part” of something?
questions.answer: It means the person sides with denial and supports it inwardly.

questions.question: What is one example of a limited negation mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Saying that something is not found in a certain location or direction.

questions.question: Why is a limited negation different from denying truths about all existence?
questions.answer: Because a limited negation deals with a narrow case that can be checked, while the other makes huge claims far beyond normal human reach.

questions.question: Which topics are included in the broad negation that cannot be proven?
questions.answer: It includes matters about this world, all beings, the hereafter, and the flow of ages.

questions.question: Why would proving such a broad denial be impossible for ordinary people?
questions.answer: Because no ordinary person can fully see all creation, all times, and the unseen world.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about people who deny very broad truths without such complete knowledge?
questions.answer: It suggests their denial is not truly established and rests on weak grounds.

questions.question: What main warning should a student take from this passage?
questions.answer: A person should not confuse rejection with knowledge, because refusing the truth is not the same as proving it false.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the real nature of unbelief that fights Islam?
questions.answer: It describes it as rooted in rejecting truth and lacking true knowledge.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the nature of belief?
questions.answer: It describes belief as a true and positive recognition based on knowledge and sound judgment.

questions.question: What contrast is made between appearance and reality in unbelief?
questions.answer: It may look like a firm belief on the outside, but inwardly it is based on negation rather than truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say lies behind the denying side of belief?
questions.answer: A real truth is behind it, either as an opening to it or as something hidden by a covering.

questions.question: What must happen before unbelief is treated as an incorrect form of judgment?
questions.answer: A person must actually accept and settle on a false negative claim as a conviction.

questions.question: What is unbelief called when there is no acceptance, no admission, and no real judgment?
questions.answer: It is called pure ignorance.

questions.question: What is the first of the two main kinds of convictions behind unbelief?
questions.answer: It is a private false belief that ignores Islamic truths and is judged to be baseless and unfair.

questions.question: Why is the first main kind set aside?
questions.answer: Because the passage is not focusing on that type in its argument.

questions.question: What is special about the second main kind of unbelief?
questions.answer: It directly resists the truths of faith.

questions.question: What is the first variety under that second kind?
questions.answer: It is not accepting the truth without forming a full judgment.

questions.question: Why is this first variety relatively easy to fall into?
questions.answer: Because a person can simply refuse agreement without having proof or a clear position.

questions.question: What is the second variety under the second kind?
questions.answer: It is agreeing inwardly with non-existence and making denial into a conviction.

questions.question: What shows that this second variety includes judgment?
questions.answer: The person sides with denial and adopts it deliberately.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation discussed after that?
questions.answer: It is denying that something exists in a particular place or on a certain side.

questions.question: Why is this first type not the main target of the passage?
questions.answer: Because it can be investigated and established in a limited way.

questions.question: What is the second type of negation?
questions.answer: It is denying broad sacred teachings that concern all beings, this life, the next life, and different times.

questions.question: What impossible condition would be needed to prove this second type of negation?
questions.answer: A person would need all-encompassing vision over the universe, the hereafter, and every stretch of time.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the deepest substance of unbelief that struggles against Islam?
questions.answer: Its deepest substance is rejection, lack of knowledge, and negation.

questions.question: What makes belief stronger in nature than unbelief, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Belief is connected to true knowledge and an affirmed understanding of reality.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat unbelief as something empty at its core?
questions.answer: Because it is based on saying no to truth rather than standing on real certainty.

questions.question: How can even the denying side of belief still serve truth?
questions.answer: It can protect truth by rejecting false ideas and pointing to what is real.

questions.question: What is the harder form of unbelief mentioned early in the passage?
questions.answer: It is the kind where people try to turn denial into something accepted as if it were knowledge.

questions.question: What is the easier form of unbelief mentioned there?
questions.answer: It is simply refusing to accept or admit the truth.

questions.question: What name does the passage give to this easier form?
questions.answer: It calls it complete ignorance without judgment.

questions.question: How many main kinds of unbelieving convictions are listed?
questions.answer: Two main kinds are listed.

questions.question: What is the first main kind like?
questions.answer: It is a false personal acceptance that ignores Islamic truths and is not the main subject here.

questions.question: What is the second main kind like?
questions.answer: It actively argues against and resists the truths of belief.

questions.question: What are the two parts of this second main kind?
questions.answer: They are non-acceptance and acceptance of non-existence.

questions.question: Which part is only a refusal to agree?
questions.answer: Non-acceptance is only a refusal to agree.

questions.question: Which part includes a committed inner choice?
questions.answer: Acceptance of non-existence includes a committed inner choice.

questions.question: Why does committed denial have to support its own claim?
questions.answer: Because once it becomes a chosen belief, it tries to justify the side it has taken.

questions.question: What kind of denial can actually be shown to be true in some cases?
questions.answer: Denial about a specific thing in a specific place or direction can be shown.

questions.question: What kind of denial cannot be shown in the same way?
questions.answer: Denial of universal and sacred truths about existence, the hereafter, and time cannot be shown that way.

questions.question: What does this teach about huge claims that faith-based truths do not exist at all?
questions.answer: Such claims are not easy to prove and would require impossible total knowledge.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly explaining about unbelief?
questions.answer: It is explaining the different forms of unbelief and why some kinds of denial cannot be proven.

questions.question: What is unbelief made of at its root, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is made of denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What is belief made of at its root?
questions.answer: It is made of knowledge, affirmation, and judgment.

questions.question: Why does the passage say unbelief only seems positive sometimes?
questions.answer: Because people may present it as a position, even though it is really built on rejecting truth.

questions.question: What positive role can a “negative” part of belief have?
questions.answer: It can uncover a true reality by rejecting what is false.

questions.question: When does unbelief count as a false judgment rather than mere ignorance?
questions.answer: When a person accepts a false denial as a settled conviction.

questions.question: What happens when there is only denial and no real acceptance of any position?
questions.answer: Then it remains simple ignorance with no true judgment.

questions.question: What is the first kind of conviction behind unbelief?
questions.answer: It is a mistaken private belief that does not take proper notice of Islamic truths.

questions.question: What is the second kind of conviction behind unbelief?
questions.answer: It is the kind that challenges and struggles against the truths of belief.

questions.question: What is the first variety inside this second kind?
questions.answer: It is non-acceptance, which means not agreeing with affirmation.

questions.question: Why is this first variety not treated as a strong intellectual position?
questions.answer: Because it contains no settled judgment and is mainly ignorance.

questions.question: What is the second variety inside this second kind?
questions.answer: It is accepting non-existence and holding denial in the heart.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying a judgment is involved here?
questions.answer: It means the person has made a decision inwardly and adopted denial as a belief.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation that the passage separates out?
questions.answer: It is a denial about one thing not being in one certain place or direction.

questions.question: Why is this first type not difficult to establish?
questions.answer: Because it is narrow and specific enough to be examined.

questions.question: Why is the second type of negation impossible to establish in the same way?
questions.answer: Because it deals with vast religious truths covering all beings, all times, this world, and the hereafter.

questions.question: What kind of ability would someone need to prove that second type of denial?
questions.answer: The person would need complete vision over the whole universe, the unseen life after death, and every part of time.
